international.title: Highly lucrative: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
international.summary: New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people • Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research. Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.
